answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on shared work, then slash that stake when independent audits show coordinated duplicate claims. A sybil operator must therefore lock real capital for every persona, while spreading control across velvet, wharf, and plume accounts does not multiply influence for free. The rule raises the cost of identities in proportion to their voting power, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
